class.name: FoliageLODLevel
class.brief_description: One level of detail inside a [FoliageLayer].
class.description: [FoliageLayer] normally holds several [FoliageLODLevel]s (e.g. a close-up LOD_0, a mid-range LOD_1, and a distant LOD_2). Each one has its own [member mesh], its own optional [member material_override], and its own visibility/fade distance range - but all levels of the same layer always share the exact same painted instance positions, rotations, and scales. [FoliagePainter3D] renders every level as its own [MultiMeshInstance3D] per cell, so at any given camera distance the renderer shows whichever level's visibility range currently covers it (and cross-fades between two levels if their ranges overlap, using a margin and [member visibility_range_fade_mode]). Levels are ordered by their position in [member FoliageLayer.lod_levels]; there is no separate index property. A level with no [member mesh] assigned renders nothing (useful, for instance, to make the farthest LOD simply disappear beyond a distance instead of showing a mesh).

members.member: If [code]false[/code], this LOD level is left out of the shadow passes. It narrows its owner's shadow setting ([member FoliageLayer.cast_shadows] or [member FoliageSpawner3D.cell_cast_shadow]) rather than overriding it, so a level cannot cast where its owner casts nothing. Turning this off for the distant levels is usually the cheapest way to make foliage shadows affordable: those levels cover most of the ground while contributing the least to what the shadow actually looks like. It is worth more still under [member FoliageSpawner3D.gpu_culling] / [member FoliagePainter3D.gpu_culling], where each shadow cascade otherwise rasterizes every camera-visible instance.

If set, overrides the material used to render this LOD level's instances (equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] on the level's internal [MultiMeshInstance3D]). Leave unset to use [member mesh]'s own surface material(s).
The [Mesh] used for this LOD level. Leave unset to render nothing while this level's visibility range is active.
Equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin]: the distance from the camera at which this level starts being visible (if greater than [code]0.0[/code]).

Equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin_margin]: how far before [member visibility_range_begin] this level starts fading in, when [member visibility_range_fade_mode] is not [constant GeometryInstance3D.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DISABLED].
Equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end]: the distance from the camera beyond which this level stops being visible (if greater than [code]0.0[/code]).

Equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end_margin]: how far before [member visibility_range_end] this level starts fading out, when [member visibility_range_fade_mode] is not [constant GeometryInstance3D.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DISABLED].

Equivalent to [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_fade_mode]: whether and how this level fades in/out across its margins instead of popping. Use [constant GeometryInstance3D.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_SELF] to crossfade smoothly with neighboring LOD levels whose ranges overlap this one's margins.
